p0.original: 关键问题：智力是一种能力还是多种能力
p0.en: Key question: Is intelligence a capacity or multiple capabilities

p2.original: 一些心理学家认为智力包含一个一般因素——g；而另一些心理学家则认为智力是多种不同能力的集合。
p2.en: Some psychologists believe that intelligence contains a general factor - g; Other psychologists consider intelligence to be a combination of diverse abilities.

p3.original: 在某一领域（如语言）展现出天分的人常常也会在其他领域（如数学或空间关系）的测验中得到高分。这一事实支持了单一、一般智力能力的说法。但也有一些明显的例外，如患有学者综合征（savant syndrome）的人。这些罕见个体拥有非凡但有限的才能，如在头脑中快速做乘法的能力，或者确定任何给定日期是星期几的能力，但他们在其他方面的心智发展迟缓（Trefert & Wallace，2002）。通常情况下，他们还会表现出孤独症谱系障碍（autism spectrum disorder）的症状（Winner，2000）——你可能已在电影《雨人》（Rain Man）中达斯汀·霍夫曼（Dustin Hoffman）塑造的这类人物的经典形象中见过这种症状。这样的个案引出了用单一的、一般的智力因素做判断存在的严重问题。显然，对于一种智力还是多种智力的问题，没有简单的答案。然而，正如核心概念所表明的，不同心理学家以不同的方式探讨了这个问题：
p3.en: Those who display talent in one area (e.g. language) often also receive high marks in tests in other areas (e.g. mathematics or space relations). This fact supports the claim of a single, general intellectual capacity. There are, however, notable exceptions, such as those with savant syndrome. These rare individuals have extraordinary but limited talents, such as the ability to multiply quickly in their minds or the ability to determine that any given date is a few days a week, but they are slow to develop in other areas (Treffert & Wallace, 2002). Usually, they also display symptoms of autism spectrum disorders (Winner, 2000), which you may have seen in the classic image of such characters in the film Rain Man by Dustin Hoffman. Such cases raise serious problems in judging by a single, general intellectual factor. Clearly, there is no simple answer to the question of whether there is one or more intellectual. However, as the core concept shows, different psychologists have addressed this issue in different ways:

p4.original: 一些心理学家认为智力包含一个一般因素——g；而另一些心理学家则认为智力是多种不同能力的集合。
p4.en: Some psychologists believe that intelligence contains a general factor - g; Other psychologists consider intelligence to be a combination of diverse abilities.

p5.original: 我们将先从心理测量领域的心理学家——那些感兴趣于开发测验来测量心理能力的人——的视角来考查这个问题。之后，我们将从认知心理学家的角度——他们为这个问题带来全新视角——来看智力。
p5.en: We will first look at the problem from the perspective of psychologists in the field of psychological measurements — those interested in developing tests to measure mental abilities. We will then look at intelligence from the perspective of cognitive psychologists, who bring a fresh perspective to the issue.

p7.original: 6.10 解释智力的心理测量理论。
p7.en: 6.10 Explain the theory of mental measurement of intelligence.

p9.original: 6.12 记住不同文化尝试理解智力的方式。
p9.en: 6.12 Remember the ways in which different cultures try to understand intelligence.

p10.original: 6.13 说出表明动物拥有智力行为和认知能力的一些研究。
p10.en: 6.13 Describe some studies that demonstrate the intellectual behaviour and cognitive ability of animals.

p13.original: 解释智力的心理测量理论。
p13.en: Explains the theory of mental measurement of intelligence.

p14.original: 心理测量学（psychometrics）是“对心理进行测量”的领域。正是心理学专业为我们提供了大部分的智商测验、成就测验、人格测验、SAT测验和各种其他评估工具。许多心理学先驱，包括阿尔弗雷德·比奈和路易斯·推孟，在为心理测量学做贡献的过程中开辟了自己的专业领域。该领域的另一个著名人物是心理学家查尔斯·斯皮尔曼（Charles Spearman），他因提出智力是单因素的理论而闻名。
p14.en: Psychometrics is the field of “psychometrics”. It is the psychology profession that provides us with most of the IQ tests, achievement tests, personality tests, SAT tests and various other assessment tools. Many psychological pioneers, including Alfred Bennet and Louis Thémon, have opened up their fields of expertise in contributing to psychological measurement. Another well-known figure in this field is Charles Spearman, a psychologist who is well known for presenting theories that intelligence is a single factor.

p16.original: 截至20世纪20年代，许多可用的智力测验都已被设计出来。英国心理学家查尔斯·斯皮尔曼（Spearman，1927）发现，个体在不同测验上的分数往往高度相关；换句话说，那些在一项测验上得高分的人通常也会在其他测验上得高分。他说，这种相关性说明，贯穿所有智力领域成绩的是一个单一、共同的一般智力因素。斯皮尔曼没有否认有些人在某些领域具有突出的才能或缺陷这件事。但是他说，这些个体差异不应该妨碍我们看到，在我们所有心理活动的背后，有一个单一的一般智力因素在起作用。斯皮尔曼称这种一般智力能力为g因子。他假定这个一般因素是与生俱来的，当时大多数心理学家也都赞同他的观点（Tyler，1988）。目前更多的研究也为g因子提供了有力的支持（Johnson et al.，2008），还找到了其重要遗传基础的证据（Haworth et al.，2010）。
p16.en: By the 1920s, many available intelligence tests had been designed. The British psychologist, Spearman, 1927, found that the scores of individuals on different tests were often highly relevant; In other words, those who scored high on one test usually scored high on the other. This relevance, he said, indicates that achievements across all intellectual domains are a single, common and general intellectual factor. Spielman did not deny that some people had outstanding talents or deficiencies in certain areas. But he said that these individual differences should not prevent us from seeing a single general intellectual factor working behind all our psychological activities. Spielman called this general intellectual ability a g factor. He assumed that this general factor was inherent and that most psychologists at the time agreed with him (Tyler, 1988). More research now provides strong support for g-factors (Johnson et al., 2008) and evidence of their important genetic base has been found (Haworth et al., 2010).

p17.original: 神经科学家也为斯皮尔曼的理论找到了一些支持证据。对g因子的各种测验都指向脑部的某些区域——特别是额叶（Duncan et al.，2000；Haier et al.，2004）。这些区域是g因子所在的区域吗？虽然有些神经科学家是这样认为的，但是其他人则认为这种解释过于简化了智力和脑的本质（McArdle et al.，2002；Sternberg，1999，2000）。总体来说，心理学家接受g因子的存在，但对它实际测量的参数和含义还有争论。
p17.en: Neuroscientists have also found some evidence in support of Spearman's theory. Various tests of g-factors point to certain areas of the brain - especially the forehead leaf (Duncan et al., 2000); Haier et al., 2004. Are these areas where the g factors are located? While some neuroscientists think so, others consider this interpretation to be an oversimplified intellectual and brain nature (McArdle et al., 2002); Sternberg, 1999, 2000. In general, psychologists accept the presence of g-factors, but there are arguments about the parameters and meanings that they actually measure.

p18.original: 6.10.2 卡特尔的流体智力与晶体智力
p18.en: 6.10.2 Cartel fluid intelligence and crystal intelligence

p19.original: 雷蒙德·卡特尔（Cattell，1963）使用复杂的数学技术确定了一般智力（general intelligence）可以被分为两种相对独立的成分，卡特尔分别称它们为晶体智力（crystalized intelligence）和流体智力（fluid intelligence）。
p19.en: The cartel of Raymond Cartels (Cattell, 1963), which uses complex mathematical techniques to identify general intelligence, can be divided into two relatively separate components, namely, crystallized intelligence and fluid intelligence.

p20.original: 卡特尔说，晶体智力包括一个人获得的知识以及获取这些知识的能力。因此，晶体智力与一个人从语义记忆中存储及提取信息的能力相关。它由词汇、算术和一般信息的测验来测量。
p20.en: According to the cartel, crystal intelligence includes the knowledge acquired by one person and the ability to acquire it. Crystal intelligence is therefore associated with a person's ability to store and extract information from semantic memory. It is measured by tests of vocabulary, arithmetic and general information.

p21.original: 相比之下，卡特尔认为流体智力是理解复杂关系和解决问题的能力——这些能力涉及算法、启发式和一般思维技能。流体智力常常由积木设计和空间可视化测验所测量，在这些测验中个体不需要通过加工某些“晶体化的”背景信息来解决问题。
p21.en: By contrast, the cartel views fluid intelligence as the ability to understand complex relationships and solve problems — capabilities that relate to algorithms, inspirational and general thinking skills. Fluid intelligence is often measured by building blocks and spatial visualization tests, in which individuals do not have to process certain “clinized” background information to solve problems.

p22.original: 卡特尔表示，这两种智力对个体适应生活都很重要。
p22.en: The cartel indicated that both types of intelligence are important for individuals to adapt to their lives.

p26.original: 20世纪后期，当认知观点作为心理学界的一支主要力量出现时，它引发了关于智力的一些激进的新观点。简言之，智力的认知观点不再只是强调用词汇、逻辑、问题解决和其他先前用于预测学业成功所测量的技能（见表6-3）。
p26.en: In the latter part of the twentieth century, when cognitive perspectives emerged as a major force in the psychology community, they gave rise to some radical new ideas about intelligence. In short, the intellectual cognitive perspective no longer simply emphasizes the use of terminology, logic, problem solving and other skills previously measured to predict academic success (see tables 6-3).

p27.original: 认知心理学家说，智力是在生活中许多方面——不只是在学校（Sternberg，2000）——取得成功背后的认知过程；因此，智力的实际范围比智力在心理测量上的概念要广泛得多。认知理论不是问“你有多聪明”，而是问“你怎么会这么聪明”。我们将主要讨论其中两个最突出的认知理论。
p27.en: Cognitive psychologists say that intelligence is the cognitive process behind success in many aspects of life, not just in school (Sternberg, 2000); Thus, the actual scope of intelligence is much broader than the concept of mental measurement. Cognitive theory asks not how smart you are, but how clever you are. We will focus on two of the most prominent cognitive theories.

p29.original: 注：不同的理论家认为智力包含不同的成分，如表中各列所示。同一行显示的是不同理论中大致相当的智力成分（不过读者应该会意识到这些对应并不准确）。例如，斯滕伯格的实践智力类似于加德纳的两种成分，即人际智力和自省智力；而斯皮尔曼的g因子则忽略了这些能力。
p29.en: Note: Different ideologues believe that intelligence contains different components, as shown in the columns of the table. The same line shows roughly the same intellectual component in different theories (although readers should be aware that these matches are not accurate). For example, the practical intelligence of Stenberg is similar to that of Gardner, i.e., interpersonal and self-critical; And Spearman's g-factors ignore these capabilities.

p30.original: 6.11.1 斯滕伯格的智力三元理论
p30.en: 6.11.1 The three-fold intellectual theory of Stenberg

p31.original: 1. 你可能会认识这样的人：这些人似乎有很多的“书本智慧”，但他们的人生并不是很成功，也许是因为他们与其他人相处得不好，也许是因为他们没有有效地处理突发事件。心理学家罗伯特·斯滕伯格说，这些人缺乏实践智力（practical intelligence）。实践智力有时被称作“街头智慧”，尽管它同样适用于家庭、工作或学校。其核心是适应所处环境和改变环境以适合自身需要，或者找到能让自己茁壮成长的环境的能力。自我意识或对自己优势和局限的认识，是实践智力的重要组成部分。
p31.en: You may know people who seem to have a lot of “book wisdom”, but whose lives have not been very successful, perhaps because they have been in poor contact with others, or because they have not been able to deal effectively with emergencies. According to the psychologist Robert Stenberg, these people lack practical intelligence. Practical intelligence is sometimes referred to as “street wisdom”, although it applies equally to families, work or schools. At its core is the ability to adapt to the environment and change it to suit its own needs, or to find an environment in which it can thrive. Self-awareness or awareness of their strengths and limitations are important components of practical intelligence.

p32.original: 2. 与实践智力相比，斯滕伯格将大多数智商测验测量的能力称为分析性智力（analytical intelligence），它依赖于问题解决、理性判断，以及对观点进行比较和对比的能力。你大学时的成绩与这种逻辑推理能力的关系可能很密切。
p32.en: 2. Compared to practical intelligence, Stenberg describes most IQ measurements as analytical intelligence (analytic intelligence), which relies on problem resolution, rational judgement and the ability to compare and compare views. Your achievements at the university may be closely related to this ability of logic.

p33.original: 3. 斯滕伯格的第三种智力是创造性智力（creative intelligence），它帮助人们产生新观点并看出概念间的新关系。创造性智力正是毕加索创造立体主义绘画形式、爱因斯坦形式化相对论时所使用的智力。它也是斯滕伯格产生他的新智力理论时所使用的智力形式。
p33.en: 3. The third type of intelligence in Stenberg is creative intelligence, which helps to generate new perspectives and to see new relationships between concepts. Creative intelligence is precisely what Picasso uses when he creates the form of stereoism and Einstein's formalization relativism. It is also the form of intelligence that Stenberg used to produce his new intellectual theory.

p34.original: 以上斯滕伯格的三部分表述通常被称作智力三元理论（triarchic theory），因为它联合了三种（tri=3）不同类型的智力。对斯滕伯格来说，每种能力——实践智力、分析性智力和创造性智力——都相对独立。换句话说，一个人在某一方面的智力并不一定代表着我们能预测出其在另外两个方面的智力。每种智力都代表着描述和评估人类表现的一个不同维度。该理论表明，把单一的智商分数看作是所有对人类心理能力重要或有价值的东西的汇总，是不正确的（Sternberg，1999；Sternberg et al.，1995）。请看表6-4，以了解斯滕伯格智力成分的一些例子。
p34.en: The above-mentioned three-part formulation of Stenberg is often called the intellectual triad (triarchic theory) because it combines three (tri=3) different types of intelligence. For Stenberg, every skill — practical intelligence, analytical intelligence and creative intelligence — is relatively independent. In other words, a person's intelligence in one aspect does not necessarily mean that we can predict its intelligence in two other aspects. Each intelligence represents a different dimension in the description and assessment of human performance. The theory suggests that it is incorrect to consider a single IQ score as a sum of all things that are important or valuable to human mental ability (Sternberg, 1999); Sternberg et al., 1995. See tables 6-4 for some examples of the intellectual component of Stemberg.

p35.original: 表6-4 斯滕伯格的智力成分的例子
p35.en: Table 6-4 Examples of the intellectual component of Stenberg

p36.original: 在这里你可以看到斯滕伯格三种智力成分包含的能力类型的一些例子。例子来源于斯滕伯格。
p36.en: Here you can see a few examples of the types of capabilities that three intellectual components of Stemberg contain. The example comes from Stenberg.

p37.original: 最近，斯滕伯格（Sternberg，2003）提出了另外一个智力元素——智慧（wisdom）。对斯滕伯格来说，智慧涉及运用智力（不论是分析性智力、实践智力或创造性智力）来实现一个共同利益而不是自私目标。例如，汽车销售员说服买家购买一辆有缺陷的汽车，可能展现出了其实践智力，而不是智慧。斯滕伯格说，只有提倡智慧，我们才能实现大多数人所渴望的社会目标。研究表明，斯滕伯格至少在一个方面可能是正确的：研究显示，智慧是晚年幸福的一个预测指标（Bianchi，1994；Hartman，2000）。
p37.en: Recently, another intellectual element, Wisdom, was proposed by Sternberg 2003. For Stenberg, wisdom involves the use of intelligence (whether analytical, practical or creative) to achieve a common good rather than a selfish goal. For example, car salesmen persuade buyers to buy a defective car, possibly showing their practical intelligence rather than wisdom. Stemberg said that only by promoting wisdom can we achieve the social goals that most people aspire to. Research suggests that Stenberg may be right in at least one way: it shows that wisdom is a predictive indicator of later happiness (Bianchi, 1994); Hartman, 2000.

p39.original: 和斯滕伯格一样，哈佛大学心理学家霍华德·加德纳也认为传统智力测验对人类心理能力的测量是有限的。但是加德纳认为，我们至少有8种独立的心理能力，他称之为多元智力（multiple intelligence）（Ellison，1984；Gardner，1983，1999a，1999b）。表6-5对加德纳的每种智力都进行了描述。现在，请花几分钟时间看看这个表。
p39.en: Like Stenberg, Howard Gardner, a Harvard psychologist, also considered traditional intelligence tests to be limited in measuring human mental abilities. But Gardner believes that we have at least eight independent mental abilities, which he calls multi-intelligence (Ellison, 1984); Gardner, 1983, 1999a, 1999b. Tables 6-5 describe each of Gardner's mentalities. Now, please take a few minutes to look at this table.

p40.original: 表6-5 加德纳的多元智力

p41.original: 加德纳声称，每种智力都产生于大脑中的一个单独模块。最后两种智力——人际智力（interpersonal intelligence）和自省智力（intrapersonal intelligence）类似于一些心理学家所说的情绪智力（emotional intelligence，有时被称为“EQ”）。情绪智力高的人善于“读懂”他人的情绪状态，也特别能觉察自己的情绪反应。
p41.en: Gardner claims that every intelligence is derived from a separate module in the brain. The last two types of intelligence - interpersonal intelligence and self-absorptionary intelligence - are similar to what some psychologists call emotional intelligence (sometimes referred to as “EQ”). People with high emotional intelligence are good at “reading” the emotional state of others and are particularly able to detect their emotional reactions.

p43.original: 认知理论对智力研究的主要贡献或许在于其提出的文化包容的价值体系：认知理论家认为，在理解智力方面，有许多出类拔萃的方式，而且一种方式未必会优于其他方式。这种观念广受欢迎。然而，这些理论的挑战在于如何评估智力：我们如何可靠地测量创造性智力、实践智力或人际智力？这些智力又能预测什么？
p43.en: The main contribution of cognitive theory to intellectual research may lie in the value system of cultural inclusion it proposes: cognitive theorists believe that there are many excellent ways of understanding intellectuals, and that one approach may not be superior to the other. This perception is widely welcomed. However, the challenge of these theories is how to assess intelligence: how can we reliably measure creative, practical or interpersonal intelligence? What do these intelligences predict?

p44.original: 在一个令人印象深刻的项目中（其本身就具有创造性和实践性），斯滕伯格与他的同事们为SAT测验开发了补充题目，用于测量创造性智力和实践智力（Sternberg，2007）。例如，为了测量创造性智力，学生要给《章鱼的运动鞋》这个题目编一个故事，或者为一个无标题连环漫画添加说明文字。还有各种旨在评估实践智力的言语和非言语问题，例如，如果你向一位教授索要推荐信，但是这个教授似乎并不认识你，你会如何回应？表6-6列出了新题目的几个例子。斯滕伯格的团队使用原创性、与背景的适配性、参与度对题目进行计分来评估创造性智力，使用可行性、适当性来评估实践智力。结果如何？新测验不仅被证明是测量创造性智力和实践智力的有效方式，它们也大大提高了学校对大一新生能否在未来取得成功的预测能力。它们也缩小了大学录取中的种族群体差异，因为测试问题的多样性能够更好地测量智力展示出的文化差异（Sternberg et al.，2006）——这也正是我们接下来要对智力进行探讨的角度。
p44.en: In an impressive project (which is itself creative and practical), Stemberg and his colleagues developed additional topics for the SAT test to measure creative and practical intelligence (Sternberg, 2007). For example, in order to measure creative intelligence, students write a story about the topic of " Smuggles ", or add an explanatory text to an untitled comic. There are also various speech and non-verbal issues aimed at assessing the practical intelligence. For example, if you ask a professor for a letter of recommendation, but the professor does not seem to know you, how will you respond? Several examples of new topics are presented in tables 6-6. Stemberg's team uses originality, contextual suitability, participation to score topics to assess creative intelligence and feasibility, appropriateness to assess practical intelligence. How'd it go? Not only have the new tests proved to be an effective way of measuring creative and practical intelligence, they have also significantly improved the ability of schools to predict the future success of the first generation. They also reduce the differences among the ethnic groups in university admissions, because the diversity of test problems is a better measure of the cultural differences shown by intelligence (Sternberg et al., 2006) — and that is precisely the perspective that we are going to look at.

p45.original: 表6-6 测量创造性智力和实践智力
p45.en: Table 6-6 Measuring creative and practical intelligence

p48.original: 记住不同文化尝试理解智力的方式。
p48.en: Remember how different cultures try to understand intelligence.

p49.original: 斯滕伯格和加德纳都认为智力的所有组成成分都具有相同的重要性。然而，每种成分的价值都是由文化所决定的，即取决于什么是一个特定社会所需要的、所奖励的，以及对其有用的。在中国，智力包括广博的知识、决心、社会责任和模仿能力等。如果你生活在太平洋岛文化中，以下哪个更重要：你的SAT分数，还是在开阔的海洋航行的能力？跨文化心理学家用这些例子让我们注意到这样的观点：“智力”在不同文化中可能有截然不同的含义（Sternberg，2000，2004）。事实上，许多语言中根本就没有我们所设想的智力——与逻辑、词汇、数学能力、抽象思维和学业成功相关的心理过程——这个词（Matsumoto，1996）。
p49.en: Both Stenberg and Gardner believe that all components of intelligence are of equal importance. However, the value of each component is determined by culture, that is, depending on what is needed, rewarded and useful for a given society. In China, intelligence includes extensive knowledge, determination, social responsibility and imitation. If you live in Pacific Island culture, which is more important: your SAT scores, or the ability to sail open seas? Cross-cultural psychologists use these examples to draw attention to the view that “intellectual” may have very different meanings in different cultures (Sternberg, 2000, 2004). In fact, in many languages there is no such word at all — a psychological process associated with logic, vocabulary, mathematical ability, abstract thinking and academic success — as we have envisaged (Matsumo, 1996).

p51.original: 斯滕伯格发现，在肯尼亚的乡村地区，实践智力最高的儿童在测量学业成功的传统智商测验中得分较低。斯滕伯格说：“在肯尼亚，高分数不会给你任何帮助。你最好去做学徒或者学习采矿、捕鱼——这些能让你养活一个家庭。”（Winerman，2005b）因此，最聪明的孩子不会去学习学业技能，而是专注于能让他们在生活中领先的实践技能。
p51.en: Steinberg found that in rural areas of Kenya, children with the highest levels of intellectual competence scored low in traditional IQ tests to measure academic success. “In Kenya, high scores will not help you. You'd better be an apprentice or a miner or a fisher -- that'll make you a family. Thus, the smartest children do not learn academic skills but focus on practical skills that enable them to lead their lives.

p52.original: 西方人假设智力与学校成功、快速解决问题有关，该假设并不具有普遍性。例如，乌干达的布干达人将智力与缓慢、深思熟虑的回应联系到一起；而研究人员在尼日尔（西非）的哲尔马人（Djerma-Sonhai）身上则发现了另一种观点：他们将智力视为社交技能和良好记忆的结合。
p52.en: Westerners assume that intelligence is linked to school success and quick fixes, and that this assumption is not universal. For example, the Buganda in Uganda link intelligence to a slow and deliberate response; In Niger (West Africa), the researchers found another perspective in Djerma-Sunhai: they see intelligence as a combination of social skills and good memories.

p53.original: 6.12.2 美洲原住民的智力概念

p54.original: 对美洲原住民所认为的有价值的心理能力，约翰·贝利（Berry，1992）进行了广泛研究。他起先让安大略省北部克里族的成年人志愿者提供给他描述思维方面的克里语词汇，从“聪明”或“聪慧”这样的例子开始。最高频率的回答大致可以被翻译为“明智”“认真思考”和“仔细思考”。
p54.en: Extensive research has been conducted into what Native Americans consider to be valuable psychological capabilities, namely, Berry 1992. He began with an adult volunteer from the Crees of Northern Ontario, who gave him the Kerry vocabulary of thinking, starting with examples such as “smart” or “smart”. The most frequent answers can be roughly translated as “wise” “thinking carefully” and “thinking carefully”.

p55.original: 智力在不同文化中意味着不同的东西。
p55.en: Intellectual means something different in different cultures.

p56.original: 尽管克里族儿童上的学校是由主流盎格鲁-撒克逊文化引入的，但克里人自己对“学校”智力和克里文化中所珍视的“良好思维”进行了区分，后者似乎以尊重为中心。正如一位受访者所解释的，智力“在印第安人的理解里就是尊重。你需要真正地了解他人并尊重他们本来的样子。”（Berry，1992，p.79）这种尊重他人的态度在美洲原住民文化中非常普遍。
p56.en: Although schools for Cree children were introduced by mainstream Anglo-Saxon culture, the Crees themselves drew a distinction between “school” intelligence and the “good thinking” cherished in the culture of Kree, which seemed to be centred on respect. As one interviewee explained, intelligence “is respect in Indian understanding. You need to really understand people and respect them as they are. This attitude of respect for others is common in Native American cultures.

p57.original: 贝利的受访者提供了一个术语，作为智力的反义的一个例子，翻译过来就是“像白人一样生活”。这个术语是贬义的，指的是克里人在一些盎格鲁-撒克逊人身上所观察到的行为。克里人将“像白人一样生活”定义为“愚蠢”和拥有“落后知识”的结合。一个“愚蠢”的人不了解生存的必要技能，也不会通过尊重长辈、聆听长辈教诲来学习。拥有“落后知识”的人会破坏人际关系、制造不和谐，而不在意与他人进行顺畅的互动，即使这种不和谐不一定是有意的或恶意的制造。例如，一位英语教师可能要求克里族学生写一篇论文来说服他人改变某些行为。然而，“说服”这个概念违背了克里文化中“接受他人本来面貌”的传统价值观。这位英语教师鼓励学生质疑长辈和传统——盎格鲁-撒克逊教育中的一种常见做法——是在鼓励学生破坏人际关系。这种做法在盎格鲁-撒克逊文化中可能是通往“智慧”之路，但在克里人的智力观中却意味着“倒退”。
p57.en: The interviewee in Bailey provided a term that, as an example of the intellectual opposite, translated as “living like whites”. The term is derogatory and refers to the acts observed by the Crees on some Anglo-Saxons. The Crees define “living like whites” as a combination of “dumb” and “downgraded knowledge”. A “soft” person does not know the skills necessary to survive and does not learn by respecting and listening to the elders. Those who possess “back-to-back knowledge” can undermine relationships, create disharmony and refrain from undisturbed interaction with others, even if such disharmony is not necessarily intentional or malicious. For example, an English teacher may require a paper from a Cree student to persuade others to change certain behaviours. However, the notion of “convincing” runs counter to the traditional values of “accepting the physical appearance of others” in the culture of Krrish. The English teacher encouraged students to question elders and traditions — a common practice in Anglo-Saxon education — by encouraging students to disrupt interpersonal relationships. Such an approach may be a path to “smart” in Anglo-Saxon culture, but it means “retrogression” in the intellectual perception of the Crees.

p58.original: 从这些例子中可以看出，不同文化对智力有不同的理解。为了理解具有不同文化传统的人并与他们合作，最“有智力”的行为或许是克制将我们自己对“智力”的定义强加于他人的冲动。
p58.en: As can be seen from these examples, different cultures have different understandings of intelligence. In order to understand and work with people with different cultural traditions, perhaps the most “intellectual” behaviour is the urge to refrain from imposing our own definition of “intellectual” on others.

p61.original: 说出表明动物拥有智力行为和认知能力的一些研究。
p61.en: Some of the studies that show that animals have intellectual behavior and cognitive abilities are described.

p62.original: 任何去过马戏团的人都可以证明，经过训练，动物能表演惊人的马戏。野生世界的狼群、狮群和虎鲸群常常会合作进行捕食和哺育幼崽。甚至你的猫也可能会使用技巧和诡计将你引向厨房，显然它是希望被投喂。但这些表现展示的是真正的思维和智慧，还是只是操作性条件反射——从先前结果中学习的能力呢？
p62.en: Anyone who has ever been to a circus can prove that animals are trained to perform amazing circuses. The wolves, lions and whales of the wild world often work together to feed and feed their cubs. Even your cat might use techniques and tricks to lead you to the kitchen, apparently it wants to be fed. But are these expressions a true reflection of thinking and wisdom, or are they merely a reflection of operational conditions — the ability to learn from previous results?

p63.original: 历史上，科学家一直认为动物的认知表现只是经过训练而习得的被伪装成智慧的简单把戏，直到珍·古道尔（Jane Goodall）等科学家陆续发布新的惊人的报告。古道尔在工作和生命方面冒着双重风险，花了30年时间在坦桑尼亚的丛林中观察和记录野生黑猩猩的行为（Goodall，1986）。她的冒险得到了丰厚的回报，她获得了大量发现，这里仅举其中一例。古道尔报告说黑猩猩会从树枝上剥下树叶，然后用树枝从白蚁巢穴中获取可口的食物。为什么这很了不起呢？她发现黑猩猩可以制造和使用工具；这是一种需要预判和计划的能力，在此之前，这一直被认为是人类区别于其他动物的能力。因此，古道尔的工作提出了人类是否具有独特性这一挑战性问题。
p63.en: Historically, scientists have thought that animal cognitive performance is simply a simple trick, learned and trained, disguised as intelligence, until scientists like Jane Goodall release new and amazing reports. Goodall, 1986, took 30 years to observe and document wild chimpanzees in the jungle of Tanzania, at the double risk of work and life. Her adventures have been rewarded with a great deal of discovery, to mention just one. Gudau reported that chimpanzees would strip leaves from branches and then use branches to obtain delicious food from termite nests. Why is this amazing? She found that chimpanzees can make and use tools; This is a capability that requires prejudicing and planning, which until then has been considered to be a human capability distinct from other animals. Thus, the Goudhor work raises the challenging question of whether humanity is unique.

p64.en: 6.13.1 Capacity to make human beings unique

p65.original: 如果不算制造工具，人类可能拥有哪些独特的认知能力？一种可能是心理理论（theory of mind）。例如，扑克玩家在虚张声势时就是在使用心理理论。对偷吃饼干盒中饼干一事撒谎的小孩也使用了心理理论。但最近的动物研究表明，低级的西丛鸦（乌鸦的亲戚）可能也会用心理理论：当一只西丛鸦为下一餐藏匿蛴螬时，如果它看到另一只鸟正在观察，那么它会稍后返回并换一个地点重新把蛴螬藏起来（Dally et al.，2005）。心理理论在黑猩猩、海豚和乌鸦身上也都得到了证实。只有人类才会运用心理理论的猜想就被推翻！
p65.en: What unique cognitive capabilities could man possess if not manufacturing tools? One may be theory of mind. For example, poker players use psychological theory when bluffing. Psychological theory was also used for children who lied about eating cookies in a cookie box. However, recent animal studies suggest that low-level West Crows (relatives of crows) may also use psychological theory: when one West Crow hides the larvae for the next meal, if it sees another bird watching it, it returns later and re-hiddles it in another location (Dally et al., 2005). The psychological theory has also been confirmed in the case of chimpanzees, dolphins and crows. Only human beings can use their psychological conjecture to be overthrown!

p66.original: 那么，也许是语言将人类与动物区分开来。但是，真为人类的骄傲感到遗憾！动物行为学家卡尔·冯·弗里希（Von Fritsch，1974）观察到，发现新花蜜来源的蜜蜂，会使用一种“摇摆舞”语言——它是沿着蜂巢内壁来表演的——来传达食物方向和距离的信息。其他科学家指出，许多动物都会使用不同的声音来传达不同的“想法”，如捕食者正在靠近。但这种动物间的交流技能有限：它们是否有资格被当作真正的语言？
p66.en: Well, perhaps language separates humans from animals. But I'm so sorry for the pride of mankind! von Fritsch, 1974 animal behaviouralist, observed that bees that found new honey sources used a “sway dance” language — which was performed along the inner walls of the hive — to convey food direction and distance. Other scientists have noted that many animals use different voices to convey different “thinks”, such as predators are approaching. But these animals have limited communication skills among themselves: do they qualify as real languages?

p68.original: 研究人员艾伦（Allen）和比阿特丽克斯·加德纳（Beatrix Gardner，1969）朝上面这个问题的答案迈进了一步。他们教一只名叫瓦苏（Washoe）的黑猩猩学习人类的语言技能，人类语言技能在以前被认为是不可能为非人类动物所掌握的。艾伦和比阿特丽克斯在瓦苏刚10个月大时收养了它，并在类似于抚养人类儿童的环境中养育它，他们教会了瓦苏使用美国手语（American Sign Language，ASL）来进行交流（Dewsbury，1996）。到5岁时，瓦苏能够做出大约160个单词的手势，而且还能将它们组成“句子”，例如，她会表示“我是瓦苏”（Me Washoe），或者请求“请再挠痒痒”（Please tickle more）。她甚至能够在陌生情境中创造新手势，例如，她第一次看到天鹅时做出了“水鸟”（water bird）的手势。而且不可思议的是，她也表现出了情绪智力：她的一位看护人在流产后请了一段时间假，当她对瓦苏打手语“我的孩子死了”来解释为什么这段时间自己没来时，报告里说瓦苏深深地望着她的眼睛，然后缓慢、小心地打出了“哭”的手语，并抚摸她的脸。当天晚些时候，到了看护人该离开的时间，瓦苏拒绝让她离开并打手语说：“请抱抱。”（Please person hug）（Fouts，1997）
p68.en: Researchers Allen and Beatrix Gardner, 1969, took a step forward in answering this question. They taught a chimpanzee called Washoe the language skills of human beings, which had previously been considered impossible for non-human animals. Alan and Beatrix adopted it at the age of 10 months in Vasu and raised it in an environment similar to that in which human children were raised, and taught Vasu to communicate in American Sign Language (ASL) (Dewsbury, 1996). By the age of five, Vasu could make some 160 gestures and could also make them into “words”, for example, she would say “I am Me Washoe” or would request “Pleace tickle more”. She can even create new gestures in strange situations, such as the "waterbird" gesture she made when she first saw a swan. And it is inconceivable that she also showed emotional intelligence: one of her caretakers took a break after the abortion, and when she explained why she had not come to the Vassut sign language, “My child is dead”, the report said that Vassou looked deeply into her eyes, then slowly and carefully struck out the “crying” sign language and touched her face. Later in the day, when the time had come for the caretaker to leave, Vasu refused to let her leave and typed in sign language, saying, “Please hold. (Fouts, 1997)

p69.original: 许多其他灵长类动物也追随了瓦苏的脚步，使用手语、各种形状的塑料代币，甚至计算机来交流。他们中的一些超越了瓦苏，拥有多达500个词汇量（Savage-Rumbaugh，1990），除了手语，他们还会对人类的声音语言做出反应（Rumbaugh & Savage-Rumbaugh，1994）。一只名叫坎兹（Kanzi）的倭黑猩猩拥有令人印象深刻的语言库，包含“明天”和“来自”（from）这样的概念词，还包含一些语法元素，如恰当地使用-ing和-ed来表示时态。一位访客答应与坎兹玩，他终于出现后，问坎兹：“你准备好开始玩了吗？”坎兹回答说：“老早准备好了！”（Past ready）（Kluger，2010）——除了语言造诣外，这也许还表现出了一种揶揄的幽默感。还有一只名叫可可（Koko）的大猩猩曾被发现用手语撒谎——这也很偶然地体现了心理理论（Patterson & Linden，1981）——甚至用美国手语来“咒骂”它的驯养员、打“脏厕所”的手语。在这一点上，大多数心理学家都相信，灵长类动物至少能够学习人类语言的基本知识，也许能达到2.5岁幼儿的水平。
p69.en: Many other primates also follow Vasu's footsteps and communicate with sign language, plastic coins of all shapes, and even computers. Some of them have gone beyond Vasu and have up to 500 vocabulary (Savage-Rumbaugh, 1990) and, in addition to sign language, they react to the human voice language (Rumbaugh & Savage-Rumbaugh, 1994). A chimpanzee named Kanzi has an impressive language base, containing conceptual terms such as “Tomorrow” and “from” and some grammatical elements, such as the proper use of -ing and -ed to express a state of affairs. One visitor promised to play with Kanz, and when he finally showed up, he asked Kanz: "Are you ready to start playing? "I'm ready for this!" says Kanz. Past ready (Kluger, 2010) — in addition to language-making, this may also be a sign of a sense of humor. Another gorilla named Coco (Koko) was found lying in sign language — and this also happened to reflect psychological theory (Paterson & Linden, 1981) — even “cursing” its tampons and “dirty toilet” sign language in American sign language. In this regard, most psychologists believe that primates can learn at least basic knowledge of human languages and may reach the level of 2.5-year-olds.

p70.original: 其他物种也能习得各种交流技能。海豚已经被教会能理解一系列的复杂手势和声音并对它们做出回应。一只非洲灰鹦鹉，能对“亚历克斯”（Alex）这个名字做出回应，它不仅会说话，还能数出最多6个物体，并且理解大小等概念，对诸如“哪个更大”这样的问题给出正确答案。一只名叫追逐者（Chaser）的边境牧羊犬也不甘落后，知道1000多个玩具名，还能根据功能和形状给它们分类（Viegas，2011）。
p70.en: Other species can also learn various communication skills. Dolphins have been taught to understand and respond to a series of complex gestures and voices. An African grey parrot that responds to the name “Alex” not only speaks, but also counts up to six objects, understands concepts such as size and gives the right answer to questions such as “what is bigger”. A border shepherd named Chaser is also indulging, knowing the names of more than 1,000 toys and classifying them according to their function and shape (Viegas, 2011).

p71.original: 6.13.3 对动物语言和智力的研究对我们有什么借鉴意义
p71.en: 6.13.3 What does research into animal language and intelligence have to do with us?

p72.original: 毋庸置疑，动物有能力做出智能行为。除了最严格的行为学家外，所有人也都会承认，许多动物都具有认知能力。这些能力对它们很有帮助：大多数动物能够很好地适应某种特定的生物生态位，这使得它们具有足够的智慧来帮助其生存。当语言被视为一个物种的适应性功能时，动物会在语言方面表现出色——以利于它们自身物种的方式而非我们人类的方式。草原犬鼠和海猫会根据捕食者的不同给同伴发送不同的信号；海豚和鲸鱼能使用声音和肢体语言来交流玩耍、捕猎和交配的欲望；甚至是低级的乌贼也会通过颜色和形状的变换来向彼此发送信息。在所有的这些方式中，动物都进行了有效的交流——这展示了物种特异的智力。
p72.en: There is no doubt that animals are capable of acting intelligently. In addition to the most stringent behaviouralists, all will recognize that many animals have cognitive capabilities. These capabilities help them: most animals are able to adapt well to a particular bio-ecological position, which gives them enough intelligence to help them survive. When languages are considered to be the adaptive function of a species, animals can perform linguistically — in a way that is beneficial to their own species rather than to our humans. Savannah dogs and sea cats send different signals to their peers depending on the predator; Dolphins and whales use sound and body language to communicate the desire to play, hunt and mate; Even low-level squids send messages to each other by changing colours and shapes. In all these ways, animals interact effectively — this shows the intelligence of species.

p73.original: 对非人类动物的语言和问题解决的研究证明，其他生物也有能力使用我们人类所定义的语言，其复杂程度令人惊讶，足以把我们拉下我们自己建构的宝座。然而，那些担心是否还能保持我们的物种优越感的人，可以从这点中得到安慰：人类语言较于其他动物语言展现出了更多的语法结构和生产力。但在某种程度上，这一发现也可能反映出我们对动物语言进行准确测量的能力是有限的。随着研究方法的进步，我们的理解也发生着演变：研究人员最近发现，有一种野生猴子能使用句法。句法是语言的一种高阶标志，被定义为按不同方式来组合语言单位（如声音或单词）以表达不同含义的能力——就像人类可以区分出“杰西给狗梳洗”和“狗给杰西梳洗”（Ouattara et al.，2009）。而且根据报告，那只叫“追逐者”的边境牧羊犬能理解名词和动词的区别。尽管人类语言能力无疑使我们比其他动物能更好地处理抽象问题，但我们必须承认我们思维视角的本质是以人类为中心的，我们也要注意自身观点和方法的局限性。
p73.en: Research into the language and problem solving of non-human animals has demonstrated that other organisms are also capable of using the language we humanly define, which is of surprising complexity enough to bring us down to the throne that we ourselves have built. However, those who are concerned about maintaining the superiority of our species can be comforted by the fact that the human language displays more grammatical structure and productivity than other animal languages. However, to some extent, this finding may also reflect our limited ability to accurately measure animal languages. Our understanding has evolved as research methods have progressed: researchers have recently found that there is a wild monkey that can use a sentence. The phrase is a high-level sign of language and is defined as the ability to combine linguistic units (e.g. sound or words) in different ways to express different meanings - just as humans can distinguish between “Jesse baptizes the dog” and “Doggies baptize the dog” (Ouattara et al., 2009). Moreover, according to the report, the border shepherd, known as the “catcher”, understands the difference between noun and verbs. While human language skills undoubtedly enable us to deal better with abstract issues than other animals, we must recognize that the essence of our thinking is human-centred, as well as our own perspective and limitations of our approach.

p74.original: 心理学很有用 测验分数与自我实现预言
p74.en: Psychology works. Test scores and self-fulfilling predictions.

p75.original: 如果你曾被认为“迟钝”“害羞”“相貌平平”“专横”或“不协调”，那么你就亲身体会过标签和预期可能具有的强大影响了。这些标签不仅能影响人们的信念，而且能影响他们的行为结果。心理学研究揭示了这个有趣的过程。
p75.en: If you were once considered to be “smuggling” “smuggling” “smuggling” or “unharmonious”, you have experienced the potential powerful influence of labelling and expectations. These labels influence not only people's beliefs, but also their behavioural outcomes. Psychological research reveals this interesting process.

p77.original: 你可能会回想起这个研究：那些被告知他们有“聪明”老鼠的学生比那些被告知他们的老鼠是“迟钝学习者”的学生会用更大的热情和鼓励来对待他们的老鼠，而这种差异实际上影响了老鼠在走迷宫等任务中的表现。罗伯特·罗森塔尔（Robert Rosenthal）与丽诺尔·杰柯布逊（Lenore Jacobson）是这项研究的领导者，他们还想知道，老师的期望是否也会对学生的成绩产生类似的影响。
p77.en: You may recall the study: students who are told they have “smart” mice will treat them with greater enthusiasm and encouragement than those who are told that they are “slow learners”, and this difference actually affects their performance in missions such as maze-walking. Robert Rosenthal and Lenore Jacobson were the leaders of the study, and they wondered whether teacher expectations would have a similar impact on student performance.

p78.original: 为了找到答案，他们给小学老师提供了关于部分学生（约占他们学生数量的20%，每个教室大约有5人）学业潜能的错误信息。具体而言，老师们被告知，一些学生已被标准测验识别为“绽放者”，在未来一年，他们会在学业上绽放光彩。事实上，测验什么也没有发现，这些“绽放者”是由实验者随机选择的。
p78.en: In order to find out the answer, they gave primary school teachers the wrong information about the academic potential of some students (about 20 per cent of them, and about five per classroom). In particular, teachers were told that some students had been identified as “breathers” by standard tests and that they would be making a difference in their studies in the coming year. In fact, no tests have found that these “breathers” are randomly chosen by the experimenter.

p79.original: 知道了老鼠身上发生了什么，你可能也能猜到教室中发生了什么。那些被老师预期能绽放光彩的儿童确实达到了老师的预期。进一步的研究找出了造成差异的4个因素（Harris & Rosenthal，1986）：老师不知不觉地为那些他们预期能够“绽放”的学生创造了更具鼓励性的氛围；给了他们更多的差异化反馈；给了他们更多的展示自己知识的机会，也给了他们更困难的工作去挑战自己。老师们认为这些儿童比其他儿童更具好奇心，也更有潜力实现人生目标。他们还认为这些儿童更快乐、更有趣、适应能力更强、更有感情、需要更少的社会认可。值得注意的是，到了年末，这些“绽放者”（实际上仅是随机选择的儿童）比那些没有得到特殊对待的学生在智商分数上获得了更大的提升。这种提升在一二年级学生中尤为明显。罗森塔尔和杰柯布逊将这种效应称为自我实现预言（self-fulfilling prophecy）。在人们达到他人或自己的期望的时候，都有这个效应的影子。
p79.en: You know what happened to rats, you might guess what happened to the classroom. Those children who were expected to be glossy by their teachers did indeed meet their expectations. Further research has identified four factors contributing to the difference (Harris & Rosenthal, 1986): teachers have unwittingly created a more encouraging atmosphere for students who they expect to be able to “breath”; More differential feedback was given to them; They were given more opportunities to demonstrate their knowledge and were given more difficult work to challenge themselves. Teachers believe that these children are more curious than other children and have greater potential to achieve their life goals. They also considered these children to be happier, more interesting, more adaptable, more emotional and less in need of social recognition. It is worth noting that by the end of the year, these “breeders” (actually only children chosen randomly) achieved a higher IQ score than those students who did not receive special treatment. This promotion is particularly evident among first and second grade students. Rosenthal and Jacobson refer to this effect as self-fulfilling prophecy. There are shadows of this effect when people meet the expectations of others or themselves.

p80.original: 在同一间教室的其他儿童身上发生了什么——他们之中是否也有人在智商分数上获得了提升？你怎么看？
p80.en: What has happened to other children in the same classroom — have some of them also gained an IQ rating? What do you think?

p81.original: 测验表明，其他儿童的智商分数也获得了提升，尽管不如“绽放者”多。然而，出现了一个出乎意料、令人不安的负相关：对于那些未被预期成才的学生来说，智商分数增长越多，老师对其有趣性和适应性的评价越低。基于此，罗森塔尔（Rosenthal，2002）警告说，预期之外的智力增长可能会引起环境中其他人的消极反应。他认为这种可能性值得进一步研究。
p81.en: Tests show that other children also have higher IQ scores, though less so than “breeders”. However, there is an unexpected and disturbing negative correlation: the more IQ scores increase for students who are not expected to succeed, the lower the teacher's assessment of their interesting and adaptableness. On this basis, Rosenthal (Rostenthal, 2002) warned that an unintended intellectual growth could give rise to negative reactions from others in the environment. He believed that that possibility merited further study.

p82.original: 来自课堂之外的自我实现预言
p82.en: Self-realization prophecy from outside the classroom

p83.original: 社会心理学家延续了罗伯特·罗森塔尔的开创性工作，将研究扩展到了课堂之外，去寻找其他环境中的自我实现预言。他们发现，在工作场所，对员工的积极期望显著提高了生产力；在军队中，积极期望甚至将绩效提高到高于私营单位的绩效水平（Kierein & Gold，2000）。在陪审团审判中，法官认为嫌疑人有罪，相较于认为其无罪，可能会向陪审团做出特定的指示——这种差异使被告被判定为有罪的可能性增加了30%以上（Rosenthal，2002）。另外，在一家小型私立疗养院开展的一项随机双盲研究发现，当护理人员对病人怀着较高期望时，病人患抑郁症的概率会大大减少（Learman et al.，1990）。显然，来自他人的预期会对我们的信念甚至行为结果产生强大的心理影响。
p83.en: Social psychologists continued Robert Rosenthal's pioneering work, extending research beyond the classroom to look for self-fulfillment predictions in other settings. They found that positive expectations of staff in the workplace had significantly increased productivity; In the military, there are positive expectations that performance will even rise to a level higher than that of the private sector (Kierein & Gold, 2000). In jury trials, the judge found the suspect guilty and may give specific instructions to the jury - a difference which increases the likelihood that the defendant will be convicted by more than 30 per cent (Rostenthal, 2002). Furthermore, a random, blind study at a small private sanatorium found that when care workers have high expectations of the patient, the likelihood of depression is significantly reduced (Learman et al., 1990). Clearly, expectations from others have a strong psychological impact on our beliefs and even on the outcome of our behaviour.
